items.body: Laufeyiar Sonr released “Tarnished” on 10 August 2026, a two-track single running five minutes and 36 seconds. It is the project’s first new material since the 2006 debut album “Vorst”, which Neuropa Records issued twenty years earlier. The title track runs 3:16 and is backed by “End of Rotation (Finitude)” at 2:20. The single is on Spotify and the usual streaming services. No label is credited on the release, and the project has no Bandcamp page. Several tracks from “Vorst” have also been added to streaming platforms under the Laufeyiar Sonr name, among them “Grey”, “White Girl”, “Through the Burren” and the two-part “Sì An Bhrù”. Those are the 2006 recordings rather than new versions; only “Tarnished” and “End of Rotation (Finitude)” carry a 2026 date. About Laufeyiar Sonr Laufeyiar Sonr is an electronic project whose only album to date is “Vorst”, released on CD in 2006 by the Belgian label Neuropa Records under the catalogue number NRP11, packaged in a 7-inch sleeve. The eleven tracks were “Grey”, “Through The Burren”, “White Girl”, “Grimhild”, “Red Bar”, “Three-Coloured Fields”, “Second Fire”, “Sì An Bhrù I”, “Sì An Bhrù II”, “The Trickster Strikes” and “Grey Park”, and Discogs lists the record under electronic, industrial, experimental and ambient. Discogs credits the project to a single member, working under the name Bastiaen Van Der Karbargenbok. Neuropa Records operated from Haaltert in Belgium and released synthwave, dark ambient and industrial records. The project’s own website is no longer online, and its only other appearance in recent years was “Through the Burren” on the compilation “Dutch Electronic Masters III” in September 2022. “Tarnished” breaks a twenty-year gap in new material.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章本质上是一篇资讯报道，介绍了电子项目 Laufeyiar Sonr 在暌违二十年后的新作发行。文章罗列了单曲的时长、流媒体上线情况，以及旧作同时上架的信息，并以大量篇幅回顾了该项目的背景：唯一专辑《Vorst》由比利时厂牌 Neuropa Records 于 2006 年以 CD 形式发行，曲目清单、成员署名、唱片分类标签（电子、工业、实验、环境）均来自 Discogs 数据库。项目唯一成员 Bastiaen Van Der Karbargenbok 的网站已下线，仅在 2022 年一张荷兰电子合辑中出现过。整篇文章未涉及任何对音乐本身的听觉分析、风格描述或艺术评价，仅记录发行事实与唱片目录信息，缺乏评论内容。

items.body: Max Meyer has not picked up a stringed instrument on stage in about ten years. The singer of the German industrial metal band Devil-M will do it twice in one weekend: he joins Italian dark electronic act Kirlian Camera as guitarist at the Fuchsbau in Chemnitz on 25 and 26 September 2026. Both nights are sold out, and the band will play a different setlist on each. Danse Macabre Records, Devil-M’s label, announced the guest appearance on 31 August. Meyer described the return to guitar as the part that stands out for him: “Nach so langer Zeit wieder mit einem Saiteninstrument auf der Bühne zu stehen, ist definitiv etwas Besonderes. Gleichzeitig ist es eine spannende Herausforderung, bei zwei Konzerten eine Band wie Kirlian Camera zu unterstützen.” In English: standing on stage with a stringed instrument again after so long is definitely something special, and supporting a band like Kirlian Camera across two concerts is an interesting challenge at the same time. He is known first as a vocalist and frontman of Devil-M, but he has worked as a multi-instrumentalist for years and is credited with drums, synths and arrangement on Devil-M records. The arrangement covers the two Chemnitz nights only. The label states that further shows or projects together are not ruled out. Kirlian Camera tour dates for 2026 and 2027 Kirlian Camera keep a single canonical calendar on their own site and warn against buying tickets for shows that do not appear on it. Seven dates are confirmed: 25 September 2026 – Chemnitz, Germany (Fuchsbau, day 1, doors 20:30, show 21:30, sold out) 26 September 2026 – Chemnitz, Germany (Fuchsbau, day 2, doors 20:30, show 21:30, sold out) 3 October 2026 – Parma, Italy (Santa Maria della Pace Church, Colonne28, “Gala in Nero – Lode”, on stage 20:30, total black dress code) 27 November 2026 – Nuremberg, Germany (Der Cult, headliner) 28 November 2026 – Karlsruhe, Germany (Die Stadtmitte, headliner) 28 February 2027 – Bruges, Belgium (De Donkerste Beurs, festival headliner) 16 May 2027 – Leipzig, Germany (Wave-Gotik-Treffen) Thirteen further entries appear on the same calendar as deliberate placeholders, with no country given. The band reveal those to their mailing list before announcing them publicly. Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027 runs from 14 to 17 May, so the Leipzig date falls on the Sunday of the festival. About Kirlian Camera Angelo Bergamini founded Kirlian Camera in Parma, Italy, in 1979, and the project became the first Italian act signed to Virgin Records. The line-up changed repeatedly through the 1980s and 1990s across a catalogue that moved between synth-pop, dark electronics, martial and neoclassical material. Elena Alice Fossi joined in 2000 as lead singer and composer, and the Bergamini and Fossi pairing has anchored the band ever since. The group have released through Dependent Records for the last three albums: “Hologram Moon” in 2018, “Cold Pills (Scarlet Gate of Toxic Daybreak)” in 2021 and the double album “Radio Signals For The Dying” on 23 February 2024. That last record runs to sixteen tracks and features Julian Assange. Side-Line covered its announcement in Julian Assange featured on new Kirlian Camera LP ‘Radio Signals For The Dying’ out in 2024 and the singles that preceded it, including “Il Tempo Profondo” and “Götter, geht weg!”. Kirlian Camera are not signed to Danse Macabre Records. The label carries the Chemnitz announcement because its own artist is the guest. About Devil-M Devil-M started in Germany in 2009 and mix industrial metal with gothic metal, with Max Meyer on vocals. Their fourth album, “Titanomachie”, came out on Danse Macabre Records in late 2025 on digital, CD and vinyl, and takes its subject from Greek myth; Side-Line covered it in Devil-M return with Greek myth album ‘Titanomachie’. Meyer has been credited across the band’s records for lyrics, arrangement, percussion and synths alongside his vocals, which is the background to the Chemnitz appearance: the guitar is not a new instrument for him, only one he has kept off stage for a decade.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的乐评，而是一则来自Side-Line的行业新闻，报道了德国工业金属乐队Devil-M主唱Max Meyer作为客座吉他手加入意大利暗潮电子团体Kirlian Camera，参与2026年9月在Chemnitz Fuchsbau两场已售罄演出的消息。文章附带大量演出日期信息以及Kirlian Camera乐队背景介绍，包括乐队1979年成立、首位签约Virgin Records的意大利艺人、近年通过Dependent Records发行专辑等履历。从内容来看，文章侧重于巡演日程公告和人事动态，缺乏对音乐本体、声音设计或创作手法的深入分析，对理解Kirlian Camera的暗潮电子美学帮助有限。整体属于信息性新闻稿而非评论文章。

items.body: Stockholm post-punk trio Then Comes Silence have released a behind-the-scenes documentary on the making of their “Judgement Day” video, filmed and edited by the Swedish video maker Marzipan Moonlight. The film follows the studio shoot for the single, which came out on 7 August 2026 through Metropolis Records as the first track from the band’s eighth album, “Requiem Ballroom”. The music video itself was directed by Damon Zurawski of Future Legend Films and staged as a live performance in a photo studio, with invited extras dancing around the band. Marzipan Moonlight’s film documents that day from the floor: the setup, the repeated takes, and the friends and members of Stockholm’s goth community who filled the room as extras. Vocalist and bassist Alex Svenson describes the shoot as closer to a concert than to a film set: “We gave a performance in the photo studio when shooting the music video. It was like a regular concert with the extras dancing around the band. People seemed to enjoy being involved in the making of this video – it’s easy to dance to and has a good dynamic.” Drummer Jonas Fransson accounts for one of the smaller participants: “We invited a bunch of friends to join us for the music video shoot, and one of them happens to be a 16-year-old Miniature Pinscher. He is almost completely deaf, so he didn’t mind walking around the studio while we were playing.” Judgement Day by Then Comes Silence “Judgement Day” is on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music. The full background to the single and to “Requiem Ballroom”, which is due on 20 November 2026 through Metropolis Records, is covered in Side-Line’s earlier report on Then Comes Silence release ‘Judgement Day’, announce album ‘Requiem Ballroom’. Svenson has described the track as a nod to Killing Joke, and Johan Lange of Agent Side Grinder plays synthesizer on one album track. Then Comes Silence tour dates The band open a European run in Belgium on 11 September and close in Stockholm in October: 11 September 2026 – Glain, Belgium – Deux Ours 12 September 2026 – Rotterdam-Albrandswaard, Netherlands – Baroeg Open Air 13 September 2026 – Rennes, France – Brewklyn 14 September 2026 – Paris, France – Le Chinois 15 September 2026 – Rezé, France – Cold Crash 16 September 2026 – Lyon, France – Rock N’Eat 17 September 2026 – Marseille, France – Le Molotov 18 September 2026 – Torino, Italy – Ziggy Club 19 September 2026 – Castelfranco Veneto, Italy – Sale Improve 20 September 2026 – Prague, Czechia – Subzero 24 October 2026 – Stockholm, Sweden – Kollektivet Livet Tickets are routed through the band’s own tour links page. About Then Comes Silence Then Comes Silence formed in Stockholm in 2012 around vocalist, bassist and songwriter Alex Svenson, who has written the lyrics and music throughout the project’s history. The line-up narrowed to a trio in 2022 and now pairs Svenson with drummer Jonas Fransson and guitarist Hugo Zombie. The band issued the self-titled “Then Comes Silence” in 2012 and “Then Comes Silence II” in 2013, followed by “Nyctophilian” on Novoton in 2015. “Blood” arrived in 2017 through Nuclear Blast, “Machine” in 2020 through Metropolis Records and SPV, and “Hunger” in 2022 through Nexilis Records and Schubert Music. “Trickery” followed in 2024 on Metropolis Records. Sonic Seducer named “Blood”, “Machine”, “Hunger” and “Trickery” album of the month on their release. The group has toured widely across Europe, North America and Latin America, sharing stages with Fields of the Nephilim, Clan of Xymox, The Chameleons and Pink Turns Blue, and has played M’era Luna, Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Amphi Festival, Castle Party and W-Festival. “Requiem Ballroom” is split into two halves, “Ballroom” and “Requiem”. Jon Bordon mixed the first, Tom van Heesch the second, and Svante Forsbäck mastered the record at Chartmakers. D.K. Griftegaard and Jonas Fransson made the cover artwork. The behind-the-scenes film is the second piece of video the band have put out around “Judgement Day”, ahead of the album on 20 November.
items._cn_summary: 该文并非乐评，而是关于瑞典斯德哥尔摩后朋克乐队 Then Comes Silence 新单曲音乐视频幕后纪录片的新闻报道。文章介绍了单曲《Judgement Day》作为乐队第八张专辑《Requiem Ballroom》首支单曲的发行信息，记录了由 Marzipan Moonlight 拍摄的幕后花絮，涵盖录音棚拍摄、邀请哥特社区好友担任临时演员等制作细节。主唱 Alex Svenson 提到该曲向 Killing Joke 致敬，鼓手 Jonas Fransson 则讲述了一只失聪的迷你品犬作为群演出镜的趣事。文中还列出了乐队即将开启的欧洲巡演日期。整体为标准化的新闻通稿格式，缺乏对音乐本身的深入评论。

items.body: And One released “Bodypop” on 1 September 2006 through Out Of Line in Europe, with a US edition following on 7 November 2006 via Metropolis Records. The ninth studio album by the Berlin electropop/EBM band turns 20 this year. It was produced by co-founder Steve Naghavi and followed 2003’s “Aggressor,” the band’s previous studio album. The German CD edition runs 12 tracks: “Mein Anfang,” “Military Fashion Show,” “Enjoy The Unknown,” “So Klingt Liebe,” “The Sound Of Believer,” “Body Company,” “Traumfrau,” “Stand The Pain,” “Sexkeit,” “Love You To The End,” “The Dream” and “Dein Ende.” A limited “Bodypop”/”Frontfeuer” CD/EP bundle added five further tracks: “Rearming Strafbomber,” “Master Master,” “A Kind of Deutsch,” “Steine Sind Steine” and “The Force.” Band members Steve Naghavi, Chris Ruiz and Gio van Oli are credited as performers on the album, which was mastered at Master & Servant. Out Of Line has since reissued “Bodypop” on vinyl in 2018 and 2023 and on cassette in 2024. Two singles preceded the album and one followed it: “Military Fashion Show” (19 May 2006), which reached number one on the Deutsche Alternative Charts, “So Klingt Liebe” (14 July 2006), which peaked at number three, and “Traumfrau” (1 December 2006). Side-Line reported on a double-vinyl reissue of “Bodypop” in 2018. About And One And One formed in Berlin, Germany, in 1989, founded by Steve Naghavi and Chris Ruiz, who met at a Berlin nightclub and initially performed under the name Body Project. Alex Two joined before the band’s 1991 debut. The single “Metal Hammer” (1990) became a club hit ahead of the debut album “Anguish,” released on Machinery Records in 1991, the year And One won a regional “Best New Artist” award. Three further albums followed on Machinery: “Flop!” (1992), “Spot” (1993) and “I.S.T.” (1994). And One signed to Virgin Schallplatten in the mid-1990s, releasing “Nordhausen” (1997), “9.9.99 9 Uhr” (1999), “Virgin Superstar” (2000) and “Aggressor” (2003). Chris Ruiz left the band in 1992 and returned in 2001; Joke Jay and Rick Schah joined the lineup across the late 1990s and 2000s. The band moved to Out Of Line for Europe and Metropolis Records for the United States starting with “Bodypop” in 2006. And One continued with “Tanzomat” (2011), “S.T.O.P.” (2012) and “Magnet” (2014), released alongside companion albums “Propeller” and “Achtung 80” as part of a “Magnet Trilogie.” Chris Ruiz left the band again in 2011 to co-found Pakt with Gio van Oli and Chad Hauger. Steve Naghavi remains the band’s constant member; Nico Wieditz has performed with the band since 2012.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非原创乐评，而是一篇关于德国乐队And One第九张录音室专辑《Bodypop》发行二十周年的纪念性新闻稿，内容以事实罗列为主：发行日期、厂牌、曲目列表、幕后人员、版本再版信息以及乐队历史沿革。文章按时间顺序介绍了乐队从1989年柏林成立至今的发展脉络，提及单曲在德国另类榜单的表现和后续黑胶、卡带再版情况，但缺乏对音乐本身的分析、创作意图探讨或美学评价。对于关注暗潮与电子音乐的听众而言，And One作为融合电子流行与EBM元素的德国乐队具备一定吸引力，但这篇文章作为纯资讯文本，信息密度集中在厂牌和曲目层面，没有提供任何关于声音设计、编曲手法或专辑艺术价值的洞见，因此作为乐评参考价值有限。

items.album: 楠瀬克昌「JAZZ KISSA 2025」世界から熱い視線を集めている日本のジャズ喫茶を美しい写真とともに紹介する一冊
items.tags: 書籍 ジャズ intoxicate 2026 June 書籍 書籍 楠瀬克昌
items.excerpt: ナショナル ジオグラフィックで特集されるなどいま世界から熱い視線を集めている日本の〈Jazz Kissa〉。そんなジャズ喫茶文化を広めるため10年も前からアクションを続けているJAZZ CITYから出版されるジャズ喫茶の紹介本であり写真集の最新版。秋田から鹿児島まで、日本全国にこれほどまでに多くのジャズ喫茶が存在することに驚愕する。それぞれの店のこだわりの音響機器と内装の美しい写真を眺めていると、どの店にも足を運びたくなり、ただのインバウンド用の案内本ではない写真集としての質の高さも感じる。この写真集を読んだ後は近くのジャズ喫茶へ行きたくなること間違いなし。
items.body: ナショナル ジオグラフィックで特集されるなどいま世界から熱い視線を集めている日本の〈Jazz Kissa〉。そんなジャズ喫茶文化を広めるため10年も前からアクションを続けているJAZZ CITYから出版されるジャズ喫茶の紹介本であり写真集の最新版。秋田から鹿児島まで、日本全国にこれほどまでに多くのジャズ喫茶が存在することに驚愕する。それぞれの店のこだわりの音響機器と内装の美しい写真を眺めていると、どの店にも足を運びたくなり、ただのインバウンド用の案内本ではない写真集としての質の高さも感じる。この写真集を読んだ後は近くのジャズ喫茶へ行きたくなること間違いなし。

items._cn_summary: 这不是一张音乐专辑的乐评，而是一本关于日本爵士喫茶文化的摄影集介绍。文章介绍了由摄影师楠瀬克昌拍摄的日本全国爵士喫茶店铺，从秋田到鹿児島，展现各家店铺独特的音响设备和室内装潢。该书由JAZZ CITY出版，旨在向世界推广日本爵士喫茶文化，曾被《国家地理》杂志专题报道。文章侧重于摄影集的视觉呈现和文化记录价值，强调其作为写真集的品质超越了普通观光指南书的范畴。与用户关注的实验爵士、电子音乐、前卫音乐等核心口味关联较弱，文章本身也偏短且更像新闻稿性质，缺乏深度的音乐评论内容。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Adam Lambert时隔约三年推出的第六张录音室作品，由Pete Nappi整体监制，声音上转向工业与重金属质感，据称反映了他青少年时期的音乐体验。合作者包括Isaac Dunbar和Lexie Liu，并采样了ATC的《Around The World》，呈现出一种怀旧未来主义的方向。专辑在流行旋律基底上加入重型电子节拍与工业元素，但整体仍属于主流商业流行框架，实验性有限。对于关注工业声响与流行融合的听众，其中部分曲目提供了可听的跨界尝试，但并未真正进入先锋或暗潮领域。

items._cn_summary: Interpol 是来自纽约的独立摇滚乐队，被乐评归为00年代中期风格的代表。文章以回忆性笔触描述了他们早期在音乐节上的舞台形象——全员黑色着装、Boss工装般的视觉风格，以及对Joy Division等后朋克前辈的迷恋。乐评指出他们刻意构建的英伦化、德式冷峻美学最终走向了自我戏仿，被戏称为sub-Editors。整体而言，这是一篇偏向怀旧与文化观察的回顾性乐评，并未深入探讨这张专辑的录音技术、编曲细节或声音美学。文章内容偏短，信息量有限，且更多聚焦于乐队的形象建构与历史定位，而非音乐本体。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — This has been sat in my playlist for well over a year by this point. I've heard it many times, but when it comes to writing a review about it, I have no idea what to say, or how to start. So here's the lowdown, released in 2005, 'The 1st Chapter' is the debut album by Norwegian progressive metal band, Circus Maximus. That's pretty much all there is to it. It's a solid album, which ticks off all the prog metal clich�s; fantastic musicianship, a singer with a powerful voice who can hit incredibly high notes, long, intricate song structures, and thoughtful, introspective lyrics. It's all here. One thing I struggled with is that there's nothing that specifically stands out that I can comment on. The music is really good and well produced, sounding a lot like Dream Theater or Symphony X (obviously), which is standard for this genre. In fact, there is one absolutely fantastic track, 'Glory of the Empire', which sounds like it could have come off of Symphony X's album 'The Odyssey', so if you like that album, you'll love this! The lyrics even have the legendary Gladiator line about "what happens in life echoes in eternity". You know the one. The absolute cheek of them! Still, lack of enthusiasm aside for my review, this is a good album. 'Sin', 'Why Am I Here', 'Biosfear', bonus track 'Haunted Dreams' and the aforementioned '?Empire' song are all worth checking out, and I've no doubt that Circus Maximus will stand out a lot more with subsequent releases.
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / neoclassical metal
items._cn_summary: 这张2005年的挪威前卫金属首专以扎实的技术功底为核心，歌曲结构繁复绵长，歌手高音能力突出，键盘与吉他交织出层次丰富的器乐段落。整体制作精良，编曲思路接近Dream Theater和Symphony X，以华丽炫技为主轴，内省歌词搭配史诗感叙事。亮点集中在《Glory of the Empire》等曲目，器乐solo段落具有一定的叙事张力。然而整张专辑基本遵循该类型的既有范式，在结构编排和音色选择上缺乏个人辨识度，更像是对前辈乐队风格的成功模仿而非突破。对于偏好前卫摇滚但尚未深入金属分支的听众来说，可以作为入门参考，但对于追求实验性、非常规结构的耳朵而言，这张唱片显得过于安全且可预测。

items.body: Review by ianjferris@gmail.com — So, right now, I'm wondering if I'm one of those "completionists" that I read about every so often; those people who just have to have everything that a band releases into the marketplace. Is that the reason that I own this album? Because when I read down through the twelve strong tracklist thereupon, I clearly see that I have exatly nine of these exact tracks on other official album releases - "Live At Knebworth", "PULSE", "Delicate Sound of Thunder" and "A Momentary Lapse Of Reason remix". The three tracks that I don't have (or should I more correctly say, the versions of those three tracks that appear here which I don't already have) are, "Marooned Jam" from The Division Bell Sessions, "Lost For Words" taken from a PULSE Tour rehearsal and an early version of "High Hopes" from the Division Bell Sessions. Of course I do have all three substantive versions of these tracks on their original album releases. So back to my original musings, am I a "completionist". No, I'm not. This is a compilation album, which brings together here twelve excellent pieces which, if I wished to hear them and them alone without this album, I'd have to fooster around selecting from different albums that I have on the shelf. I put this album on every so often specifically because these tracks are the ones that I want to hear. And a small bonus (very small bonus) is the fact that a version of three of the twelve are not available to me in my collection. So, conclusion..... I'm not a "completionist". I'm an ordinary fan who loves this compilation and I'm giving it five stars because that is what this music deserves.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑汇集了平克·弗洛伊德1987年至2019年间的后期作品片段，收录十二首曲目，其中九首来自《Live At Knebworth》《PULSE》《Delicate Sound of Thunder》等已有专辑的重复曲目，另外三首为《The Division Bell》录音室时期的未发行版本，包括"Marooned Jam"、排练版本的"Lost For Words"以及"High Hopes"的早期混音。整体而言，这张选辑并非新创作内容，而是将散落于各张专辑中的零散曲目集中呈现，方便乐迷一次性聆听。对于已拥有相关专辑的听众而言，重复内容较多，仅少数未发行素材具有一定收藏价值。作为主流摇滚厂牌发行的汇编作品，与实验、前卫、电子或暗潮等口味关联较弱。

items.body: This is French cellist Astrig Siranossian’s fifth release on the Alpha label, and her earlier albums cover a wide-ranging repertoire in which she appears both as a chamber musician and as a soloist. Here she is joined by the London Symphony Orchestra and François-Xavier Roth for Elgar’s Cello Concerto, with Britten’s Cello Sonata, Bruch’s Kol Nidrei and Elgar’s Salut d’amour completing the program. Cello Concerto Amazon Presto Apple There are some ninety readily available recordings of the Elgar Cello Concerto, so Siranossian is entering a crowded field. Every new release is measured against Jacqueline du Pré’s legendary performance with Barbirolli and the LSO (Warner Classics), and that status is well earned — I know of few other concerto recordings in which the solo part is played with such overwhelmingly personal, emotional expression. Barbirolli’s accompaniment is just as involving. But it is fascinating to hear Elgar’s own 1928 recording with Beatrice Harrison (the composer conducting the New Symphony Orchestra, Warner Classics), where his less heart-on-sleeve leadership has a different but potent emotional effect. Recent performances tend to fall into two contrasting interpretive camps. Some are gentler and more emotionally restrained, such as Paul Watkins/BBC Philharmonic/Davis (Chandos), Gautier Capuçon/LSO/Pappano (Erato), and Daniel Müller-Schott/Oslo Philharmonic/Previn (Orfeo). Others embrace a more extroverted emotional approach like du Pré’s that is nevertheless their own, such as Pieter Wispelwey/Netherlands Radio Philharmonic/van Steen (Channel Classics), Steven Isserlis/Philharmonia/Paavo Järvi (Hyperion), and Johannes Moser/Suisse Romande/Manze (Pentatone). Siranossian’s interpretation falls into the latter category. Her playing, caught up close by Alpha’s engineers, draws a dazzling range of colors from the 1756 Gennaro Gagliano cello. Siranossian’s interpretive ideal is signaled in the opening recitative: marked fortissimo and nobilmente, the initial attack is ferocious and emotionally raw, the nobilmente honored through color and weight rather than any stiff-upper-lip reticence. Her first statement of the main theme is silvery and lithe, while the later restatement is full-toned and impassioned. The second movement (Lento – Allegro molto) brings a delicate, playful lightening of mood, answered by an Adagio of greater intensity, the playing more inward and contemplative, the cello’s color at times blanched and exhausted. The final movement returns to a more unreserved, impassioned manner, surveying darker regions of the score that others leave unexplored. The LSO, which has played this score more times than anyone can count, strives to match Siranossian’s intensity, but is sometimes hampered by Roth’s more objective leadership. There is compensation in hearing the score laid out with such transparency, allowing us to appreciate the craft of Elgar’s writing. Astrig Siranossian. I last wrote about Britten‘s Cello Sonata in a review of Sheku Kanneh-Mason’s 2025 Decca recording. That reading, like this one from Siranossian and pianist Nathanaël Gouin, a regular duo partner, leans into the tough modernity of Britten’s writing. If the Kanneh-Mason siblings find more playfulness in the second-movement Scherzo, Siranossian and Gouin more thoroughly uncover the darker musings of the third-movement Elegia, albeit at a significantly faster tempo. The Marcia lacks the menace Johannes Moser finds (with pianist Paul Rivinius, Hänssler), but the closing Moto perpetuo has ferocious momentum and drive, without eclipsing the unique energy and bravado of Rostropovich’s account with the composer (Decca). Bruch‘s Kol Nidrei is built around two Jewish melodies. The composer described the first as “an age-old Hebrew song of atonement”; the second, in D major, draws on “O weep for those that wept on Babel’s stream,” a song he called moving and truly magnificent. The only performance of the work I own is János Starker’s with the LSO led by Doráti (Eloquence). It is quite lovely, both pained and calming. Siranossian’s slightly slower reading is more sweetly voiced and more openly poignant. Elgar’s Salut d’amour makes a perfect digestif. Alpha’s engineering is excellent, and it is particularly good to hear the LSO away from the acoustically challenged Barbican Hall; the concerto sessions took place at LSO St Luke’s. The liner notes consist of a January 2026 interview in which Siranossian spends more time on what connects her cello (once owned by John Barbirolli) with the repertoire on the album than on the music itself. Nevertheless, after hearing this recording I intend to hear Siranossian’s earlier albums — recommended. items.body: Most of these songs have been sitting on Bandcamp one at a time since 2020. Music for the basses, the first Xavier Monax album to reach streaming services, brings twelve of them together and runs 42 minutes. The French solo project, which works under the lower-case name monax, describes the record as melancholic material in an indie rock and post-punk style. It went up on Spotify, Apple Music and Deezer on 30 August 2026; the artist gives 18 September as the date it lands on all platforms. The title is of course a wink to Depeche Mode’s “Music For The Masses”. The running order is “The Call”, “Is it the stars”, “White rooms”, “14 off”, “Don’t shoot the pianist”, “Leaving the darkness”, “Quiet again”, “Ordinary Fields”, “Follow me”, “Back in town”, “The sound from my mind” and “From here”. Every track had already appeared as a standalone Bandcamp release between November 2020 and April 2026, so the album works as a first collected edition rather than a set of new recordings. It is self-released, with no label and no distributor beyond digital delivery. About Xavier Monax Xavier Monax is a solo project from France. The Bandcamp page gives the country and nothing more precise; there is no city, no biography text and no listed website or social account. Releases are billed as Xavier Monax on streaming services and credited to monax in the liner text. The Bandcamp catalogue is the fuller picture: around 37 items, mixing short albums with a long run of individual tracks. The earliest, “tout est à vendre”, carries a 2003 date. “The John Room Innocence” followed in September 2020 and the single “Music for the Basses” – one track, “Don’t shoot the pianist” – in November 2020. The nine-track “Viral Kiss” arrived in June 2022, “DREAMS 23” in April 2023 and the two-track “Sur le sable” in April 2025. Between those, singles appeared at a steady rate: “The Sound Of My Mind” in October 2022, “14 off” in February 2023, then “Back in town”, “Ordinary Fields”, “Refuges”, “Simon”, “White rooms”, “Follow me” and “Leaving the darkness” across 2024, “From Here” and “Quiet Again” in 2025, and “L’ironie du sort” and “Is it the stars” in 2026. Cover versions of Johnny Cash’s “Hurt” and of Tristana sit alongside them. The project tags its own work as alternative, alternative rock and wave, and has no recorded label history, no announced live dates and no press coverage in any language before now. “Music for the basses” is the first Xavier Monax release to appear outside Bandcamp.

items.body: Mike Watt returned his bass part within a day. That track now sits at the centre of “Emotional Plea”, the debut single by Work Crush, the new project of Hudson, New York songwriter Stephen Bluhm. The electropop and disco-leaning single was released on 28 August 2026 and is available on Bandcamp. Bluhm wrote the music and lyrics and handled vocals, guitar and synth. Watt, co-founder of the San Pedro punk band Minutemen, plays bass. Alex Wernquest contributed drums and percussion and shares the recording and mixing credit with Bluhm. The track was recorded and mixed at Basement Floods Records in Catskill, New York, with Watt’s bass recorded at Studio tHUNDERpANTS in San Pedro, California. Jeff Lipton mastered it at Peerless Mastering in Boston, with Costanza Tinti as assistant mastering engineer. Musician and illustrator Steve Teare drew the cover, a child playing with a toy military plane. Emotional Plea by Work Crush Why Work Crush wrote ‘Emotional Plea’ The song is a first for Bluhm, who had not written directly about politics before. He explains what pushed him to it: “With Emotional Plea, I’d never written an overtly political protest song, but I felt I couldn’t ignore in my writing what’s happening around us, with ICE, with Gaza, with the complacency and lack of compassion.” The recording came together faster than his usual pace, and Watt’s involvement is the reason he gives for that. “I usually write slowly, but this came together quickly because I felt it so urgently,” Bluhm said. “Mike Watt is one of the funkiest bass players I know, and I knew he’d be perfect for the song. I’m grateful he agreed. He sent his bass track back within 24 hours. The man works furiously.” Musically the single sets a steady dance rhythm under synthesizers and clipped rhythm guitar, with Bluhm singing in a baritone. He describes the project’s method in one line on its release page: “At Work Crush, we believe all kinds of messages and stories can be told through the fine art of disco.” The same note states that no generative AI was used on the release. About Work Crush and Stephen Bluhm Work Crush is the current project of Stephen Bluhm, a songwriter based in Hudson, in New York’s Hudson Valley. Bluhm began releasing music under his own name, issuing the self-titled album “Stephen Bluhm” on 17 September 2017. “Easter” followed on 14 April 2023. His second full-length, “Out of the Nowhere. Into the Here.”, came out on 19 April 2024, recorded, mixed and produced by Bluhm with guest players including musicians from Bard College’s The Orchestra Now and the Bard Conservatory Orchestra. It is built around strings, horns, flutes, piano and reeds rather than synthesizers. An instrumental version of the album was released alongside it. “Emotional Plea” is his first release since that album and the first under the Work Crush name. It moves him from orchestral chamber pop to a synth and dance-rhythm setting, with two collaborators he has worked with before, Alex Wernquest and Steve Teare, and one new one in Mike Watt. No further Work Crush releases have been announced.
items._cn_summary: 这是关于Stephen Bluhm新项目Work Crush首支单曲《Emotional Plea》的新闻类报道，而非乐评。歌曲定位为electropop与disco风格，由Bluhm本人撰写词曲并演唱、演奏吉他与合成器，前Minutemen成员Mike Watt担任贝斯手，Alex Wernquest负责鼓与打击乐。作品以稳定的舞曲节奏为底，铺设合成器与切分吉他，Bluhm以男中音演唱。创作动机源于对当前政治局势的有感而发，是Bluhm首次尝试直接书写政治抗议主题的作品。录音在纽约Catskill的Basement Floods Records完成，贝斯部分由Watt在加州San Pedro的Studio tHUNDERpANTS远程录制。文章内容以信息发布为主，缺乏对音乐本身的深度分析。整体风格偏向主流独立流行，与实验、前卫或暗潮等偏好领域距离较远。

items.body: Februus is the ancient Roman god of putrefaction and cleansing. Symbolically, a figure's fiery dome alludes to rampant mental activity, psychological distress, or enlightenment. The firey-headed two gentlemen on the cover art of Construction of Conflict (illustrated by Daniel Karlsson) are probably undergoing some divine spiritual awakening in the presence of that god. The Swedish one-man progressive death metal act Februus aren't strangers to the concept of the flaming noggin: last year, they released a short EP, The Crushing Pressure of Oppressive Thought, featuring a similarly-suited man with what seems to be his brain floating above him with a trail of flames. But can the project's death metal truly melt one's face?Februus is the work of solo member Andreas Karlsson juggles vocals, guitars, bass, synths, and drum programming—no wonder his head's on fire! He associates with tough-to-play genres, supposedly techdeath blended with progressive metal, but sonically, his artistic choices are questionable. While technically professional, Construction of Conflict is produced incredibly unharmoniously, which would make sense if Karlsson aimed for a dissonant death metal record, which it may as well be. His vocals are echoed close to beyond audibility, and the drums follow suit. Can you fathom how loud everything has to be for the drums—on a progressive/technical death metal album—to be mostly undetectable? Only during thrashy segments like the near-end of "The First Limb is Cut" or, at their fullest, during the jazzy instrumental interlude "The Misery That Awaits the World" can you truly detect the drums, and I'm not as disgruntled as I should be at the fact of their programming, since I can't hear them anyway.I'll reiterate it once more: the guitars on this album are LOUD. Riff-forward instrumentation is key to Februus' style, and the riffs sure are friggin' forward. Karlsson is a guitar maestro, able to both noodle with care (see "Fueled by Narcissism" for a lovely, lengthy solo) and wank around (see the aforementioned song's closer for chiptune-adjacent blasts) concisely, but there are better ways of proving this than with noxiously blaring mixing. On denser compositions like "Measures of Escalation" and "Suppressing the Future," the atmosphere is simply draining because of its overwhelming levels of chugging. Most of these stouter cuts' efforts to ease the conditions by way of a waltzy, guitar-led component or a jazzy break, but the "recorded in an alleyway" effect strips these additions of their supposed relief. I'm sure Karlsson had great intentions with these features, but they can't distract from the glaring production job. These segments are also the only times his bass and synths are tended to; two instruments that could contribute plenty to the record's atmosphere if it weren't for their sonic exclusion. After a solid forty-and-a-half minutes, you'll acclimate to Februus's mixing job, and you may even find it endurable. But beginning the album is quite difficult, and your precious headphones need to be 5% lower than what you think. Otherwise, Andreas Karlsson is going to immolate your brain. Construction of Conflict by FEBRUUS
items._genre: progressive death metal / technical death metal
items._cn_summary: Construction of Conflict 是瑞典单人项目 Februus 的全长专辑，Andreas Karlsson 一人包揽人声、吉他、贝斯、合成器及鼓编程，定位为技术死亡金属与前卫金属的融合。专辑以密集的 riff 为核心驱动力，吉他演奏在细腻独奏与炫技段落之间切换，并穿插华尔兹式吉他段落与爵士风格器乐间奏作为喘息空间。然而，乐评指出混音制作存在严重问题——吉他音量过大、鼓声几乎不可闻、人声回响过度，导致整体声场失衡，厚重的 riff 段落变得沉闷压迫，削弱了器乐编排本应带来的层次感与氛围营造效果。贝斯与合成器仅在少数段落中被听见，未能充分发挥对氛围的贡献。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由三位多伦多音乐人远程合作完成，十八首短小曲目仅用三十四分钟便结束。编曲以拨弦吉他与尤克里里为核心，辅以键盘和滑棒吉他，营造出温暖而简约的音色氛围。人声清澈高亢，有时略显脆弱，歌词围绕失去与宿命感展开，呈现出淡淡的忧郁与幽默。曲目风格跨度较广，开篇的蓝调民谣、灵魂乡村、Twangy乡村摇滚各有特色，其中最短的一首仅一分二十秒，以极简方式表达完整意象。整体听感如梦中之乐，柔和、内省、富于情感层次，是一张工艺精致但风格偏向传统民谣的作品。
